our_argument_summary: WIN-053 (Two-pole geomagnetic model). Verdict: Self-Contradicted. The dome's toroidal architecture is topologically a ring magnet, in which flux conservation forces a ~1,600:1 magnitude asymmetry between source and return — yet the dome's fitted B(r) gives near-equal coefficients A=62,376 nT and C=64,852 nT, a 1,660:1 self-contradiction within the dome's own geometry. Independently, the exponential B ∝ e^(−r/λ) form is justified post-hoc rather than derived from the toroidal architecture; A, C, and λ are observed pole values relabeled; λ is the same parameter pressed into service for an unrelated phenomenon (firmament height H(r)). c12 verifies the ISS-1245 pickup integration: detail_evidence paragraph 0 now explicitly invokes ∇·B=0, calls the fitted form a "monopole pair" (two same-signed sources, not source+sink), and frames the topology mismatch as an independent failure surviving even if magnitude is set aside.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard geomagnetism (WMM2025, IGRF-13, CHAOS-7) explains both pole magnitudes (~55,000 nT at each geographic pole) plus full multipolar structure including the South Atlantic Anomaly from a degree-13 spherical harmonic expansion grounded in geodynamo physics, achieving ~50 nT RMS globally (~0.1%). The dome's 20% RMS corresponds to ~11,000 nT — 200× worse — and the two-parameter exponential cannot reproduce any localized anomaly. The dome is relabeling the same observed magnitudes (geodynamo origin) as aetheric toroidal flow.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: A = 62,376 nT (13% above observed 55,000 nT at the geographic north pole) and C = 64,852 nT (18% above observed 55,000 nT at the geographic south pole) are fits to long-published WMM/IGRF surface-observatory values. No derivation from disc_radius, firmament_height, or any dome geometric property is provided. λ = 8,619 km is the same scale length used for the firmament H(r) function in WIN-002/061 — borrowed verbatim with no independent derivation. Trivial-transcription post-hoc.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: Per dome's own pages, A, C, λ are stated as fit results, not derived from disc_radius=20,015 km or firmament_height=9,086 km. The toroidal architecture only constrains B(r) to have two peaks, which any two-aperture topology would produce — not uniquely diagnostic of the dome's claimed geometry. Our detail_evidence captures this: "a two-peaked surface fit is what any closed two-aperture topology would produce, so even this minimal predictive content is not uniquely diagnostic of the dome's specific toroidal architecture."

holes_found.description: The new paragraph 0 sentences invoke "monopole pair" as a label for the e^(−r/λ) functional form. Strictly speaking, a textbook magnetic-monopole field has Coulomb-like 1/r² spatial dependence, not exponential decay. The "monopole pair" framing in the integrated text is correct topologically (two same-signed sources, no sink) but conflates sign structure with spatial form. A pedantic defender could nibble: "exp(−r/λ) is not the field of a monopole pair; it is an arbitrary phenomenological decay law." The underlying ∇·B = 0 argument doesn't depend on the spatial form — it depends on the sign structure of A and C — so the prose is operationally correct, but the "monopole pair" label is rhetorical compression of "topology of two same-signed sources without a sink."
holes_found.recommendation: Optional one-clause clarification when introducing the "monopole pair" framing: "— a label that refers to the topological sign structure (two same-signed sources, no sink), not to the 1/r² spatial form of a true monopole field; the spatial-form objection misses the topological point that ∇·B = 0 forbids two co-signed apertures in any closed circuit." Severity minor; existing text holds operationally.

stronger_arguments.description: The 1,660:1 flux-conservation discrepancy is geometrically robust across the entire plausible aperture range. Sensitivity sweep (quantitatively verified this run): aperture 500 km → 1,666× short; 1,000 km → 416× short; 3,000 km → 46× short; 10,000 km → 4× short. For the dome's fit to be flux-consistent, the polar aperture area would need to EQUAL the disc area (ratio = 1) — i.e., the entire 20,015-km disc would have to be the polar aperture, which is geometrically meaningless because the disc IS the return. There is no aperture choice that rescues B_south = 64,852 nT under flux conservation. Our text already presents the 500/1000/3000 sweep; an optional addition would name the geometric upper bound: "no aperture geometry satisfies flux conservation short of A_pole = A_disc, which collapses the source/sink distinction the toroidal architecture requires."
sources: Geometric: π × r_pole² ≤ π × R_disc² = 1.258×10⁹ km² requires B_south_required ≥ 62,376 × (r_pole/R_disc)²; setting B_south_required = 64,852 gives r_pole = R_disc, the geometric upper bound.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's recognition that a single-pole field model cannot reproduce observed dipolar geomagnetism is sound physical reasoning, and represents a genuine V50.6 → V51.0 improvement (wins.json:053 detail_verdict_text — "The dome's toroidal geometry is a genuine improvement over V50.6's monopolar model — recognizing that a single pole cannot explain a dipolar field shows sound physical reasoning"). The closed two-aperture circuit framework is at least topologically right about the broad structure: any closed magnetic flux circuit DOES require two terminations (source + sink), and the V51 dome architecture (Axis Mundi + Antarctic Sump) at least posits that pair-structure where V50.6 had only one pole.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Positing the correct topology framework is not the same as predicting the field within it. The dome's implementation violates the very flux conservation law its closed circuit invokes (wins.json:053 detail_evidence — "the 1,660:1 discrepancy within the model's own geometry"). The fitted coefficients overshoot observed pole magnitudes by 13–18% (A=62,376 vs 55,000 = +13.4% verified this run; C=64,852 vs 55,000 = +17.9% verified this run) but only when treated as positive surface magnitudes — under the closed-circuit topology the dome itself claims, the southern coefficient should be a sink (~39 nT) not a source (~65,000 nT). The detail_verdict_text captures this as "the refinement made the model quantitatively worse on its own terms" — V51 created a new self-contradiction (closed-circuit flux conservation) that V50.6's simpler monopolar model could not have, because a monopolar model has no return path.

deeper_analysis:
The c11→c12 delta is the ISS-1245 pickup — adding monopole-pair / ∇·B=0 framing to the main argument paragraph (paragraph 0) of detail_evidence, where previously this topology framing was buried in the third-rescue rebuttal. This is the right structural move: the topology argument is the stronger claim (it does not depend on aperture-size assumptions) and now sits in paragraph 0 alongside the magnitude argument, instead of as a back-end rebuttal to a specific defender pivot. The new sentence "The dome's formula is not merely off by a factor of ~1,660 — in its algebraic form it is the field of two same-signed magnetic monopoles rather than of a closed dipolar circuit, an independent topological failure that survives even if the magnitude discrepancy is set aside" is exactly the two-independent-paths-to-self-contradiction framing that strengthens the WIN-053 case: even granting the defender every aperture-geometry assumption, the sign structure of A>0 and C>0 in the fit form forbids a closed dipolar circuit. The tldr_verdict simplification (HTML anchor → plain text §6.1) is cosmetic and unobjectionable. The third charitable reading's (ii) sub-paragraph also got the inclination-data tightening (c11 H#1's recommendation) — text now explicitly says "measured field inclination at the geographic poles points oppositely — inward at one pole, outward at the other — so a magnitude-only re-interpretation still requires designating one aperture as the flux sink." c11 H#1 is RESOLVED.

The one genuinely-new minor this cycle is the "monopole pair" spatial-form vs sign-structure pedantry — small but worth flagging because a defender who knows EM textbooks will note that exp(−r/λ) is not the true monopole 1/r² form. The operationally-correct topological argument doesn't depend on the form, so this is a rhetorical-compression issue, not a factual error. Two minor c11 carry-overs (H#0 aperture-area-ratio sentence; H#3 ISS-1245 monopole-pair label in prose) are now in different states: H#0 still pending (not lifted into prose); H#3 RESOLVED (the new paragraph 0 sentences are the integration). H#2 (editorial numbering) appears silently resolved — current sequence is (1)/(2)/(3) consistent, no orphan "fourth."

advocate_mode.best_defense: A dome defender accepting our six methodological principles could mount the following: "WIN-053 is presented as a PHENOMENOLOGICAL fit, not a first-principles derivation. The code_analysis tag derives_from_dome=false is already a stated property of the WIN — we are NOT claiming A, C, λ are derived from dome geometry; we are fitting coefficients to surface observations. The 1,660:1 self-contradiction only bites if you assume B(r) is a flux density that must satisfy ∇·B=0 around the closed circuit. The dome's actual claim is much weaker: B(r) is the magnitude-projection at the dome SURFACE of an aetheric flow density; the aetheric flow itself satisfies its own conservation laws (aetheric continuity, not Maxwellian ∇·B), and what we measure as magnetic field is the Maxwellian-instrument projection of that flow. Under this reading, A and C are surface-measurement magnitudes whose positivity is just a notational convention for surface-flux density; the source-sink directional structure lives in the underlying aetheric flow, not in B(r) signs."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Already foreclosed in current detail_evidence (wins.json:053): "A second retreat — claiming the toroidal flow is aetheric rather than Maxwellian, so ∇·B = 0 does not apply and flux conservation is simply inapplicable — is the defender's strongest remaining move, but it abandons the very claim WIN-053 rests on. Once interior flux conservation is waived, no derivation links A, C, or λ to the toroidal geometry: B(r) demotes to a three-parameter surface fit to observed pole magnitudes... and the toroidal geometry does no numerical predictive work beyond dictating that the fit must have two peaks — and a two-peaked surface fit is what any closed two-aperture topology would produce, so even this minimal predictive content is not uniquely diagnostic of the dome's specific toroidal architecture." The aetheric-non-Maxwellian defense is already explicitly named and dispatched. Defense rated 2 (trivially refuted by existing text).
